claim_text: The public MCP surface is an 11-tool spine (9 analyzers + plan_checks -> finalize_deliverable) plus a deterministic, non-blocking review_before_final facade = 12 public tools total; 7 leaf checks are internal. The spine is hidden-by-default behind CT_EXPOSE_ALL: by default tools/list advertises ONLY review_before_final (default discovery surface = 1), and CT_EXPOSE_ALL=1 advertises all 12 (CT_DISABLE_FINALIZE then composes to drop finalize_deliverable -> 11). Hiding is discovery-only; tools/call still dispatches all 12 handlers. The facade's per-task-type checklists are also exposed as 6 reusable MCP prompts.
CT-MCP wins 30/30 (and 42/42) defect scenarios vs baseline.
The real-agent value pilot is a null/toy result: ceiling was task difficulty, not model strength.
In the pilot, 5 numeric false-blocks occurred vs 1 (partly lucky) grounding win — net-negative friction.
Deterministic checks cannot verify semantic correctness (e.g. a wrong method that self-traces passes the gate).
CT-MCP reduces high-severity defects by forcing checkable intermediate artifacts and rejecting answers that violate objective contracts.
Phase 4 will run a 4-arm ablation (A/B/C/D) to isolate whether artifact binding is the active ingredient.

CT-MCP detected the planted defect in 42/42 hand-crafted defect scenarios with 0/14 false positives on the clean controls (detection quality of the tools in isolation; baseline/prompted comparison pending a real-model run).
Phase 1a will wire a real model into benchmark/runner.ts, eliminating the synthetic baseline/prompted rows so a measured vs-baseline / vs-prompted comparison becomes reproducible.

On output-level injected defects (deterministic bundle mutations), the settled gate blocks 100% (106/106 mutants) with 0% false-block (0/41 correct bases) and 100% precision; blocker_code_accuracy 27.4% (wrong-number caught as drift, fabrication as span-mismatch). Output-level (section 8) only; repair, task-level mutation, and live-workflow product value are NOT proven by this.

The 100%/0% injected-defect result measures the gate as a deterministic validator of structured defects; it does NOT establish that CT-MCP reduces defects in live model workflows (the B track showed Sonnet and Haiku both ~0% natural defect density). Workflow value is the open question for the Phase 4 ablation.

Claude Haiku 4.5 natural high-severity defect density is 0.000 (Wilson 95% [0,0.026], n=144 failure-prone), measured on the fixed grading instrument as arm-agnostic plain generation. From this it is INFERRED (not separately measured) that a 4-arm A/B/C/D natural ablation is inconclusive/all-tie-high (no natural defects for any arm to prevent); the 4-arm run was pre-registered as optional and NOT executed. The 0.000 density is proven; the 4-arm tie is an inference.

On a DIRECTIONAL repair pilot (6 bases x 4 arms, single-defect drafts, Haiku, 1 sample/cell, NO confidence interval), the gate showed no repair advantage: arms WITHOUT the gate repaired 6/6 (A generic feedback) and 6/6 (C self-review); arm B (structured gate feedback plus binding) repaired 4/6 (its 2 losses were finalize-loop no_answer truncations, not bad feedback) at 3-11 turns vs A/C 1 turn; D (forced artifacts, no binding) 5/6. B raw 0.67 clears the pre-registered 0.50 absolute bar but is NOT a gate-attributable win (A/C=6/6). Pilot-grade, not powered.

No MEASURED binding benefit on a strong model (DIRECTIONAL): A5 (n=2 correct-answer probes) showed Haiku produces faithful derivations with no answer-to-artifact drift to catch, and on the repair pilot (n=6) forced-artifacts-WITHOUT-binding (D, 5/6) at-least-equals forced-artifacts-WITH-binding (B, 4/6). binding_attributable_catch is INFERRED near 0, NOT directly measured; n=6 cannot separate binding-inert from binding-too-costly (B losses were truncations; D one loss was a genuinely wrong answer). Consistent with the pre-registered B-equals-D legitimate null.

Phase 4 narrows CT-MCP value on strong models, with UNEVEN evidence strength: the deterministic CATCHING result is fully powered (recall 1.0, false-block 0 on n=147 injected bundles, CI-backed); the no-repair-value and no-binding-benefit conclusions are DIRECTIONAL pilots (n=6, no CI). So catches-every-planted-defect is well-evidenced; no reasoning/repair/binding improvement and the 3-11x token cost of the spine are a strong-but-pilot-grade signal consistent with all other evidence. The C-approx-B / B-not-greater-than-D kill fired directionally.

On the Phase-5 host-contract corpus, ct-enforce (single host-side call) gives perfect separation on the curated set: 16/16 violating deliverables REJECTed (false_release_reduction 1.0, Wilson 95% [0.806,1]) and 0/14 contract-satisfying deliverables blocked. On the live arm a real agent shipped host-contract violations at natural_violation_rate 3/9 = 0.33, so the false-release opportunity is real, not theoretical. Scope: curated arm deterministic; live arm small n (6 satisfies + 3 violations gradeable, 5 unparseable).

The Phase-5 friction that fired the kill rule (realism_false_block 1/6 = 0.167 and spine_required true) traced ENTIRELY to one over-specified contract (fin_numeric_dag, task_type numeric_analysis + evidence_level rederived, which hard-requires a numeric_derivation DAG and arithmetic_checks). The same total-must-equal-X requirement authored as a host == constraint (fin_total_reconcile) RELEASEs the good-faith single-shot deliverable spine-free AND REJECTs a wrong total, proven deterministically in the curated arm. The gate was not too strict; the contract was over-specified. Fix = contract-authoring guidance, no gate change.

ct-enforce is a LOW-FRICTION host release gate (good-faith single-shot deliverables RELEASE, no multi-turn spine) when contracts are authored per docs/designs/HOST_CONTRACT_AUTHORING.md (value/field/format requirements as constraints/must_include; evidence_level rederived reserved for genuine independent re-derivation). As-run with the anti-pattern contract the frozen kill rule fired on friction; a corrected re-run (anti-pattern re-authored as a == constraint, gate UNCHANGED) DEMONSTRATES ship_worthy=true: realism_false_block 0/7=0.0, spine_required false, false_release_reduction 1.0, natural_violation_rate 0.125. Caveat: 6/14 grounding-heavy deliverables were unparseable single-shot (an agent/prompt limitation the review_before_final facade artifact mode addresses, not a gate defect); gradeable n=8. This is host-contract FALSE-RELEASE reduction, distinct from and not evidence for reasoning/repair improvement (Phase 4 closed those).
